title: Evaluating a source (RADAR)
intent: formative · pattern spot-the-error / source-evaluation · judge one lens at a time
statement: Same source, a different lens. Work RADAR — Relevance, Authority, Date, Appearance, Reason — one check at a time, and stamp a verdict on each.

source.title: “Why Solar Will Power Everything by 2027”
source.meta: greenfuturenow.blog · no author listed · posted 2019 · no citations

items.label: Relevance
items.question: fits your need?
items.verdict: A popularising overview — on topic, but too shallow for a literature review.

items.label: Authority
items.question: who made it?
items.verdict: No named author on a self-published blog — no credentials to trust.

items.label: Date
items.question: current enough?
items.verdict: Posted 2019; its 2027 forecast is already overtaken — stale for a fast-moving field.

items.label: Appearance
items.question: well-produced, referenced?
items.verdict: Readable but unreferenced — no data, no sources to follow up.

items.label: Reason
items.question: why was it made?
items.verdict: To persuade and win clicks, not to inform — read the slant.

steps.title: Meet the source
steps.text: Before judging, see what you are dealing with. Work the five RADAR lenses in order.

steps.title: R — Relevance
steps.text: Does it fit your actual need, at the right depth? On topic is not the same as useful.

steps.title: A — Authority
steps.text: Who made it, and what makes them credible? An anonymous blog has none to offer.

steps.title: D — Date
steps.text: When was it written or updated, and does recency matter here? An overtaken forecast is a warning.

steps.title: A — Appearance
steps.text: Is it well-produced and referenced — data, citations, structure? Polish is not proof; references are.

steps.title: R — Reason
steps.text: Why was it made — to inform, or to persuade and sell? Name the motive before you trust it.

steps.title: Reach a verdict
steps.text: Weigh the five together. RADAR and CRAAP reach the same place by different routes: relevant, but not reliable.

feedForward.text: Relevant but not reliable — it fails Authority and Appearance and is out of Date. Use it only to illustrate hype, and corroborate every claim with peer-reviewed or official data.
